root_cause.text: The drivers/pci/endpoint/functions/pci-epf-ntb.c and pci-epf-vntb.c functions epf_ntb_init() call alloc_workqueue() without verifying its return value, so if memory allocation fails, the null workqueue pointer is later dereferenced by queue_work() in epf_ntb_epc_init().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a NULL check for alloc_workqueue() and returns -ENOMEM immediately after allocation, preventing use of a NULL workqueue. The CVE description and commit message state that "alloc_workqueue() can return NULL on memory allocation failure" and "this may lead to a NULL pointer dereference when queue_work() is later called with the NULL workqueue pointer in epf_ntb_epc_init()."

vuln_statements.explanation: This line assigns the result of alloc_workqueue() without checking if it returns NULL. If memory allocation fails, kpcintb_workqueue will be NULL, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when used later in queue_work().
Continuation of the alloc_workqueue() call. The return value remains unchecked, so a failed allocation yields a NULL workqueue pointer that is stored and later dereferenced.

This line registers the driver without verifying that the workqueue was successfully allocated. Consequently, if alloc_workqueue() failed, the driver continues to be used, and a NULL workqueue pointer may be dereferenced during device binding.
Same vulnerability as in pci-epf-ntb.c: the return value of alloc_workqueue() is not checked for NULL. A failed allocation leads to a NULL workqueue pointer stored in kpcintb_workqueue.
Continuation of the alloc_workqueue() call in the vntb variant. No NULL check on the return value, so a NULL pointer may be passed to queue_work() later.

Driver registration proceeds unconditionally after the unchecked alloc_workqueue() call. This allows the use of a potentially NULL workqueue pointer when the driver binds to a device, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
PCI: Add WQ_PERCPU to alloc_workqueue() users

Currently work items enqueued by schedule_delayed_work() use "system_wq"
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 78f5d0d5a23dd81106cbe999d9dcd522964a8f1a
Author: Marco Crivellari <marco.crivellari@suse.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 7 15:25:26 2025 +0100

    PCI: Add WQ_PERCPU to alloc_workqueue() users
    
    Currently work items enqueued by schedule_delayed_work() use "system_wq" (a
    per-CPU wq), while queue_delayed_work() uses WORK_CPU_UNBOUND (used when a
    CPU is not specified). The same applies to schedule_work() that is using
    system_wq and queue_work(), that makes use again of WORK_CPU_UNBO
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit only adds the WQ_PERCPU flag to alloc_workqueue() but does not add a NULL check for its return value. The code still assigns the result to kpcintb_workqueue and proceeds to pci_epf_register_driver() without verifying that the workqueue was allocated successfully. This matches the vulnerability root cause: missing return value check leading to potential null pointer dereference.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the epf_ntb_init() function, `alloc_workqueue()` is called without checking its return value (line ~2108). If it returns NULL (memory allocation failure), the global `kpcintb_workqueue` remains NULL. Later, `queue_work()` and `queue_delayed_work()` are called with this pointer in `epf_ntb_epc_init_interface()` and `epf_ntb_cmd_handler()`, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. The commit does not include any fix such as a NULL check or error handling for the workqueue allocation.
